**Observations:**
- Affected part: Leaf (tomato plant)
- Visual features: Dark brown to black necrotic lesions with a distinctive **ring/circular pattern** — multiple concentric or circular ring-shaped spots scattered across the leaf surface
- The spots appear to have blurred/diffuse margins rather than sharp edges
- Lesions are bronzed/dark brown-black with some areas appearing as rings or ring-within-ring patterns
- Leaf remains green otherwise; no powdery coating, no velvety mold, no V-shaped pattern

**Reasoning:**
- The concentric ring patterns on leaves with blurred margins strongly match **Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (TSWV)** — "bronzing on upper leaf surfaces, distinct necrotic spots" with "lesions caused by TSWV have blurred margins, whereas lesions from other diseases have definite margins"
- The circular/ring-shaped dark necrotic lesions with indistinct edges are classic TSWV symptoms
- Early Blight has concentric rings too but lesions are larger, darker brown, with very defined edges and typically start on lower/older leaves
- Septoria has smaller spots with dark pycnidia centers — not matching
- The blurred ring pattern across the leaf surface is the key diagnostic indicator pointing to TSWV
